01 · The Wild Instinct

Built on the bird wolves actually hunted.

Long before there were bags of kibble, wild turkey was one of the few animals abundant and vulnerable enough to be a staple kill across most of the wolf's range — a real part of the ancestral diet, not a marketing invention. It's also, by biological luck, one of the gentlest proteins a modern dog can eat: turkey is far less likely than chicken, beef, or dairy to set off the immune reactions behind itchy skin, ear infections, and upset stomachs, which is why vets often reach for it first when a dog's diet needs a reset.

1Protein source in this entire recipe — no blends to react to
LowReactivity, compared to the chicken and beef most dog foods default to
WildOrigin — turkey has been prey to canids since long before domestication
02 · The Cold Chain

Cooked once. Frozen fast. Never cooked again.

Freeze-drying pulls water straight out of food as vapor, never through more heat — the closest a bowl can get to what a wolf would have torn into, minus the risk of raw. Everything that survives slow-cooking and prep gets locked in place at the freezer, not boiled off later.

Hr 0

Slow-cook & prep

Turkey is gently cooked through; organs, vegetables, legumes and raw kale are prepped whole.

Hr 2

Batch & blend

Everything is combined in small batches — no purees, no fillers, no rendered meat meal.

−40°F

Flash freeze

The batch is frozen solid within hours, locking the recipe in place before anything degrades.

90 sec

Rehydrate & serve

Add warm water and it's back to a fresh-cooked texture in under two minutes, bowl-ready.
